# Whitespace in font family names

Original XML generated by `tools/font_name_spaces_fixture.py`. The reference
application exported the unchanged source to the one-page PDF. Record glyph
origins with `python tools/reviewed_font_reference.py font-name-spaces`.
The JSON binds source and PDF by SHA-256. No font files are redistributed.

The reference application resolves leading/trailing ordinary spaces and a trailing nonbreaking space
in these family names. Arial, Times New Roman and Courier New variants have
exactly the same PDF glyph origins as their corresponding canonical names.
Arial bold italic controls confirm style selection is retained. Source family
spellings remain intentionally distinct in the DOCX.

The browser checks exact pairwise glyph equality, native baseline differences
below 0.2pt, editing, undo, and export/reopen. Font availability tests cover shared
loading, alternatives, bundled-font resolution, and symbol encoding. Family
normalization applies only to display lookup, never to stored declarations.

Open precision issue, unrelated to whitespace: the canonical browser glyph
origins differ from this native reference PDF by up to 0.205pt for Arial, 0.639pt for Times
New Roman, 0.086pt for Courier New and 0.280pt for Arial bold italic. The paired
whitespace variants have exactly the same drift as their canonical controls.
These controls establish name resolution, not complete font-shaping conformance.
